name: Verifiable digital identity wallets
summary: Digital identity wallets hold issuer-verified credentials so people can prove facts such as age, licence status or identity with controlled disclosure.
useCase: You prove that you meet an age threshold or hold a valid licence using a wallet, without sending a full scan of your identity document to every service.
whyNow: The EU framework and national deployments are moving credentials from pilots into consumer applications. Italy’s Documenti su IO reached more than 5.3 million unique users since launch by June 2025 and more than 10 million activations by February 2026. These are adoption signals for an initial national service, not a count of fully interoperable EU wallets. A wallet is useful only when trusted issuers provision credentials and enough services accept them. Privacy, selective disclosure, account recovery, device security and fraud handling all affect practical adoption. A deadline to make wallets available does not mean citizens use them frequently or that every relying party is integrated.

mainstream.scope: Routine use of interoperable digital credentials in participating EU public services and selected financial, travel and age-verification workflows; other regions follow different schedules.
mainstream.rationale: Existing national adoption provides a base, while the EU rollout obligation supports issuer and service integration. Several years may be needed after availability for routine acceptance and reliable cross-border operation. Uneven implementation, difficult recovery processes or low service acceptance can keep actual usage below the headline number of issued wallets.

metric.name: Italy Documenti su IO uptake
metric.scope: Italy’s initial national digital-document service, a precursor within the IT-Wallet system.

points.status: reported lower bound: unique users since launch

metric.limitations: The releases use different labels: unique active users since launch versus activations. Neither is a monthly-active-user count. The service initially supports specific national documents and is not a measure of complete cross-border EU wallet adoption. No CAGR is appropriate.
metric.futureNote: No defensible comparable external deployment forecast found. The separate maturity path is an analyst scenario, not measured adoption.
metric.growthLabel: National service: >5.3m users → >10m activations; definitions differ

milestones.text: The European Commission proposed the European Digital Identity framework, starting the current policy and interoperability cycle.
No harmonised annual EU consumer wallet-usage observation was identified; the framework was still developing.
The EU’s first four large-scale wallet pilots began in April, testing cross-border use cases and ecosystem participation.
The digital identity regulation entered into force in May; Italy made three digital documents available to all eligible IO users in December.
Italy reported more than 5.3 million unique users of Documenti su IO since its December launch, as of 3 June.
Italy reported more than 10 million activations in February. The EU end-2026 availability requirement remains a deadline at the October cutoff, not evidence that all countries have completed rollout.

tailwinds: Governments and regulated issuers can supply trusted credentials with broad utility.
A common framework can reduce repeated document collection and verification work.
Selective disclosure can improve privacy when implemented and accepted correctly.
bottlenecks: Availability, activation, repeated use and acceptance are four different adoption measures.
Interoperability includes legal trust, credential formats and operational support.
Recovery, accessibility and fraud resistance must work for people beyond early adopters.
watchMetrics: Monthly active credential presentations and successful service completion, not downloads alone.
Number of accepting public/private services and cross-border transaction success.
Fraud rates, recovery completion, user abandonment and the amount of personal data disclosed per check.
